text: What proof should the CFO require before any AI savings appear in the board deck?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
" That discipline needs to become a formal gate, not just a one-time correction. Here's the proof standard I'd put in front of the board deck before any AI savings number appears: (1) Operational KPI first, dollars second.
Cycle-time improvement (KPI /) must show a measured delta from the 16-day baseline before any dollar conversion happens. The loaded evidence is explicit: dollarize only after an owner-approved throughput model, not before. (2) Owner sign-off on the conversion model. Finance Controls is listed as the owner role for the core value KPIs.
The CFO should require that owner to sign the assumption set — deflection rate, handling minutes, FTE cost — before a dollar range goes on a slide. The rework reduction range ($480K–$950K) and status-inquiry deflection ($180K–$420K) are wide enough that an unsigned model is a board-level credibility risk.
(3) Evidence status must be source_backed, not review_required. 9M) — are flagged review_required, not source_backed. Those numbers cannot go in a board deck in that state. The Liquidity forecasting automation and Finance support agent are source_backed; those can travel.
